title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
concepts: write-ahead-log: append-only log of changes written before applying them
leader-follower-replication: one node accepts writes and streams them to replicas
multi-leader-replication: several nodes accept writes and reconcile conflicts
leaderless-replication: clients write to several replicas and read with quorums
quorum-reads-writes: overlapping read and write sets guarantee freshness
replication-lag: delay before a follower reflects the leader's writes
read-your-writes-consistency: a user always sees their own updates
consistent-hashing: partitioning keys so few move when nodes change
partitioning-by-key-range: splitting data into sorted key ranges
secondary-indexes-partitioning: local versus global indexes across partitions
lsm-trees: log-structured merge trees for write-heavy storage
b-trees: page-oriented balanced trees for indexing
column-oriented-storage: storing each column together for analytics
schema-evolution: changing encodings while keeping compatibility
acid-transactions: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability
snapshot-isolation: each transaction reads a consistent snapshot
write-skew: anomalies from concurrent decisions on stale reads
two-phase-commit: coordinating an atomic commit across nodes
linearizability: operations appear to happen at one instant
consensus: getting nodes to agree on a value despite faults
exactly-once-semantics: effects applied once despite retries
change-data-capture: streaming a database's changes to other systems
event-sourcing: storing state as an immutable log of events
batch-vs-stream-processing: bounded versus unbounded data processing

sponsorship: senior people actively opening doors for others
staying-aligned-with-authority: keeping leaders informed to keep trust

the-staff-project: owning a long, ambiguous, high-impact effort
glue-work: the invisible coordination that keeps teams shipping
getting-in-the-room: earning a seat where decisions get made
operating-at-staff: balancing coding, mentoring and organizational work
promotion-packets: documenting impact for a staff promotion
finding-sponsors: building relationships that advocate for your work
work-on-what-matters: choosing problems with leverage over busywork
influence-without-authority: leading through persuasion not hierarchy

systems-thinking: modeling organizations as stocks and flows
technical-debt-migrations: running migrations that actually finish
de-risk-migrations: proving a migration on the hardest cases first
work-on-the-backlog: falling-behind, treading-water, repaying, innovating
succession-planning: preparing others to take over your role
career-ladders: explicit expectations for each level
performance-calibration: comparing assessments across managers
